title: PR automation config (.github/pr-automation.json)
description: Read by every tool in tools/ through tools/pr-config.mjs, which merges this file over its defaults and refuses unknown keys and unsafe values. Every field is optional; the defaults are shown. Paths and patterns are JavaScript regular expressions as strings.

defaultBranch.description: The branch PRs merge into. Keep it equal to the repository's default branch (the setup script warns if it isn't) and to `on.push.branches` in pr-bot.yml and postcommit.yml.

title.description: The PR title, which becomes the commit subject: `[Area][Sub-area] Qualifier: Title Case Summary`.

areas.description: Allowed first tags. Empty: any one capitalised word.

maxTags.description: How many [Tag]s a title may have: the area, then sub-areas. 0: no tags at all (then `areas` must be empty).

qualifiers.description: The word before the colon. Empty: no qualifier.

titleCase.description: Book-title case: small words lower case unless first or last.

imperative.description: Refuse summaries that start "Added", "Fixes" and the like.

example.default: [UI] Fix: Keep the Menu Open after a Click
example.description: Shown in the error for a malformed title; make it pass your own rules.

branch.description: PR branch names, checked by pr-policy and (for `user` and `prefix`) enforced at creation by the branch-names ruleset where rulesets are enforced.

pattern.description: user: `<GitHub username>/<short-name>`, the username the PR author's; prefix: `<one of prefixes>/<short-name>`; regex: matches `regex`; any: not checked.

exempt.description: Branch names accepted whatever the pattern. The submodule bump branches are exempt by themselves.

requiredSections.description: `## Section` headings that must have content.

pastTenseSections.description: Sections whose bullets should start with a past-tense verb (a warning only).

sensitivePatterns.description: Extra things no description may contain, besides personal paths, GitHub and AWS tokens, and private keys. `what` names it in the error, e.g. "a customer's name".

testing.description: The Testing section: the author's own results, for the head they're about (the "Tested at" model, README.md).

requireTestedAt.description: Require `Tested at <sha>` for the PR's head, or a commit with the same changes (tools/same-changes.mjs).

localChecks.description: Lines the section must have, each a bullet or paragraph matching `match` with a result ("12 passed, 0 failed", "30 of 30 suites passed", or "skipped: <why>"). With `paths`, only for PRs that change a matching path, and `why` says so in the error.

forbidden.description: Files no PR may add or change (matched case-insensitively against each path).

message.default: look like credentials or private keys. Never add them; rotate any that were pushed.
message.description: Follows the list of matching files in the error.

method.description: How the bot merges. squash and merge commits get the guideline message (title, blank line, PR URL); rebase keeps the PR's commits.

status.description: The commit status the bot keeps on each PR's head. `<status>-update` marks the default branch's commits it brought the PRs up to date with.

requiredChecks.description: Check-run (job) or status names that must pass on the head before the bot merges.

ciApprovals.description: For PRs that change `ciPaths`: a PR's own workflows run from its files, so it could weaken what checks it.

ciPaths.description: Also never rebuilt by the bot.

approverAssociations.description: Review author_association values that count as write access.

carryApprovals.description: An approval of a commit that makes exactly the same changes as the head (a clean rebase someone pushed): count it and say so in a comment; post an approval review that says whose it carries (needs Actions allowed to approve PRs); or never carry it. The bot's own rebuilds keep approvals in every mode.

rebuild.description: Keeping open PRs up to date: after every merge the bot replays each behind PR's own commits onto its new base (stacks bottom up), as data, and pushes with a lease.

checkWorkflows.description: Workflows the bot dispatches on a branch it pushed (its push starts no pull_request runs). `withPr`: the workflow takes a `pr` input.

reviewDelayMinutes.description: After a rebuild, the bot reviews again this many minutes later, once those checks have had time to finish.

requiredChecks.description: The status checks the default-branch ruleset requires (from GitHub Actions). Only the bot's status by default: checks a dispatch ran (on a PR the bot rebuilt) don't satisfy a ruleset's required checks, and the bot requires merge.requiredChecks itself.

staleDays.description: prune-branches deletes branches with no open PR and no commit for this long (and merged ones).

keep.description: Branches the bot never deletes or rebuilds. The screenshot branch is kept by itself.

hold.description: A ready PR with this label isn't merged (or rebuilt).

extra.description: More labels for the setup script to create (e.g. for issue forms).

precommit.description: What precommit.yml runs on every PR, with a read-only token.

scripts.description: npm scripts to run, in order, e.g. ["lint", "test"].

runTests.description: Run tools/run-tests.mjs (every standalone suite in test/, these tools' own included).

postcommit.description: Module: postcommit.yml checks the merged commit's message and runs precommit's steps on the default branch, after each merge (the bot dispatches it after its own) and weekly.

screenshots.description: Screenshots: the description rule (requiredFor) and the module (screenshots.yml runs your script on the PR's base and the PR; screenshot-comment.yml compares and comments).

requiredFor.description: Paths whose change needs a Screenshots section with an image (or, with the module on, "See the Screenshots comment").

script.description: The npm script that writes `<view>.png` files into $SCREENSHOTS_DIR (an empty directory). It gets $SCREENSHOT_VIEWS, the views below, comma-separated.

install.description: An npm script to run first (e.g. one installing a browser). Empty: none.

views.description: The views the script should take, in the order the comment shows them. Others it writes are shown after them.

branch.description: Where the images are stored (auto/pr-<n>/...). Never pruned or rebuilt by the bot.

pruneDays.description: Images of PRs closed this long ago are deleted, daily.

limits.description: Bounds on the untrusted artifact: views per side, bytes per image and in all, and pixels per image decoded.

pages.description: Module: GitHub Pages from the default branch, with a preview of every other branch. Every preview is public and runs unreviewed code on the site's origin (README.md).

previews.description: Publish branches other than the default one under previewDir/<branch>/.

include.description: What to publish: files, and directories ending with /.

entry.description: A branch without this file isn't published; a preview's gets the preview meta tag.

previewMeta.description: <meta name> holding the branch name in a preview's entry file.

submodules.description: { "path/in/repo": "https://host/owner/repo.git" }: submodules to publish, fetched at the pinned commit from this URL, never the branch's .gitmodules.

stale.description: Module: stale.yml, daily: closes inactive PRs and prunes branches.

closePrs.description: Close PRs with no activity for `days` (actions/stale), labelled `label`; `exemptLabel` keeps one open. Their branches go with the prune.

submodules.description: Module: update-submodules.yml, daily: pushes each moved submodule's bump to its branch and links "open the pull request" in the run summary. A person opens the PR.

title.description: The PR title, one line without double quotes, $ or backslashes; {sha} is the new commit. Make it pass your title rules.

localPreviews.description: Module: tools/serve-branches.mjs (`npm run serve:branches`), local branch previews: every branch of a remote at /<branch>/, read straight from git, on 127.0.0.1. The private alternative to Pages previews. Flags (--port, --fetch, --remote, --host, --repo) override these.

remote.description: The remote whose branches (refs/remotes/<remote>/*) are served.

fetchSeconds.description: How often to `git fetch --prune` the remote. 0: never (fetch yourself).

entry.description: A branch is listed only if its tip has this file, and /<branch>/ opens it.

submodules.description: Submodule paths to serve at the commit each branch pins, from the submodule's clone (fetched from its own remote when the commit is missing), e.g. ["lib/theme"].

marker.description: If set, every HTML page gets <meta name="<marker>" content="<branch>"> after <head>, so the app can tell a preview, and which branch, from the real site (e.g. to keep its storage keys apart). Empty: pages are served as they are.

types.description: Content types by extension, over the built-in list, e.g. { ".glb": "model/gltf-binary" }. Unknown extensions are application/octet-stream.
